howItWorks.heading: From HH file to precise diagnosis
howItWorks.step1Desc: Upload the .txt file from any tournament (PokerStars, GGPoker, ACR or CoinPoker). Multiple files supported at once.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Each decision is evaluated by equity, position, and MTT/SNG context. The detection engine crosses frequency with impact, and shows you exactly what's costing you chips.
howItWorks.step3Title: Improve with focus on what matters
howItWorks.step3Desc: Study plan built on your own error patterns, not generic content. Track progression through the 7-level system.

features.heading: Why GrindLab is different
features.f1Title: Your real data, not generic theory
features.f1Desc: The diagnosis is built on your own tournaments. Every identified leak exists in your real history, not in a textbook range.
features.f2Desc: ICM, M-ratio, tournament stage, and bubble. The engine evaluates every decision with the right tournament context, not isolated cash-game equity.
features.f3Desc: Study cards generated from your own error spots, plus an AI Coach that talks through your hands, not generic content.

plans.heading: Simple and transparent
plans.details: Start free. Upgrade based on how often you play.

faq.heading: Before you upload the first file
faq.q1: Which sites can I import from?
faq.a1: PokerStars, GGPoker, ACR (WPN) and CoinPoker, from the tournament .txt file. You can drop several at once. If you also send the tournament summary, finish place, prize, ROI and field size come in: that is what makes final table detection possible.
faq.q2: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a2: No. Everything runs in the browser, including the replayer. There is no program to install and no HUD to configure at the table.
faq.a3: It is not a solver interface, and it does not try to be. The reference answer for each decision comes from our own solve, and the platform's job is to apply it to YOUR hands: where you deviated, how often, and what it cost.
faq.q4: How do I know the diagnosis is not the AI guessing?
faq.a4: Because it is not an opinion: it is error counting in your own history. A leak only becomes "proven" once the improvement survives the confidence interval, and it reopens on its own if the mistake comes back in your real hands.
faq.q5: Can I try it without paying?
faq.a5: Yes. The Free plan is permanent and asks for no card: 2 tournaments per month, 15 analyses and 5 on-demand GTO solves. One tournament is already enough for the first leak to show up.
faq.q6: Does it work for cash games?
faq.a6: The focus is tournaments. ICM, M-ratio, stage and bubble go into every decision, and that context is exactly what changes the right answer compared to cash.

demo.b2: The recommended action, side by side with yours.

prova.heading: Every trainer measures drill accuracy. We measure at the table.
prova.sub: Getting a drill right proves little: you learn that the answer there is fold, not when to fold. What matters is what happens in your next tournament.
prova.c1Title: Measured in your play, not in a simulator
prova.c1Desc: After you train a leak, the platform tracks hands of that type in the tournaments you import and compares them with your earlier history.
prova.c2Title: Only claims it when it survives chance
prova.c2Desc: Improvement becomes "proven" only when the difference survives the confidence interval. Until it does, the screen says it cannot tell yet. That is on purpose.
prova.c3Title: Reopens by itself if you regress
prova.c3Desc: If the mistake returns in your real hands, the leak reopens even if you keep acing the drill. That is the case that exposes memorising without transfer.
prova.nota: None of this is an AI opinion about your game. It is error counting on your own history, with the confidence interval in plain sight.

b2.titulo: Every verdict says where it came from
b2.texto: Each decision is judged by the solver, the ranges or the engine, and the card says which. When we have no basis, it states the reason instead of inventing a number.

b3.texto: The study plan points at where you bleed the most and training opens right there. Spaced repetition on what you got wrong, with the grid and the cost beside it.
